"or" as an appositive restatement of one value in another unit ("9.05 points, or 0.94 percent"): the Disjunction section would wrongly make this an opaque (Or …)
degree/extent adverb modifying a VERB ('weakened slightly'): Degree is defined as (Degree <entity> <scale> <level>) on an entity plus an adjective scale, with no event-degree form
Minimizing degree adverbs ("little", "hardly", "barely"): the Degree rule keeps the positive property and records the adverb as a level, which misstates a near-negative.

a sentence-final reporting clause ("..., Jones said") and its scope - the instruction set covers only matrix-first "X said that P", and does not say whether a postposed attribution seals the preceding clause(s) under Theme or leaves them asserted at top level, nor how far left its scope reaches across a semicolon

clause-level participial complex prepositions ('based on X', 'according to X', 'due to X'): the reduced-relative rule covers participles post-modifying a noun, and the -ing preposition list (during/pending/notwithstanding) does not reach these

Delta / change-of-value measures ("was up 5.91 points", "fell 3 percent"): Measure and MeasureAtLeast/AtMost record absolute values and MoreBy needs two named relata, so a bare rise or fall has no licensed carrier.
magnitude of a change/decline ("was off 1.07 points") — no licensed scale or head for a delta as opposed to a level

"be up/down N <unit> to <value>" — a change in a measured value over time, with a delta and a resulting level; Measure, MeasureAtLeast/AtMost, MoreBy and TimesAs all relate entities on a scale and none encodes one entity's value moving by an amount to a new value

Absolute 'with NP V-ing' adjunct ('with GE shares edging 7 cents lower'): the 'with'-phrase rules cover only comitative CoAgent and Instrument NPs, so the clause is asserted at top level with no relation at all to the matrix reacting event.
Differential comparative with an implicit standard ('edging 7 cents lower'): MoreBy requires an explicit 'than Y' to fill its second argument.

a non-factive prediction whose content is carried by an NP complement ('predicted sales of between $6.9 billion and $7.5 billion') — sealing is finite-clause-only, so the predicted range ends up asserted as top-level fact rather than as the content of the prediction

clause-level "following NP" as a temporal adverbial — the instruction set's only mention of `following` groups it with participial post-modifiers that must be reduced-relative events, which would be wrong for this adjunct use
appositive/equivalence "or" ("107.08 points, or 1.3 percent") — Disjunction treats every "or" as inclusive-disjunctive, with no form for a restatement of the same value

a delta / change-in-value measure ("closed up 42.56 points") — Measure records an entity's level on a dimension and MoreBy compares two entities, so one entity's change across time has no licensed form and is indistinguishable here from a level
an index or price level reported by "closed at N" with no stated gradable adjective or dimension noun
the magnitude of a CHANGE ('fell 5/32'; 'taking its yield to 1.23 percent from 1.16 percent') — no licensed form for a delta, nor for one entity's value moving between two time-indexed levels
a free participial adjunct of result (', taking its yield to ...') — the participle rules cover post-modifiers on nouns, not a clause-level adjunct with the matrix clause as its implicit subject
change in a measured value ("lost 11/32 in price", "to 3.21 percent from 3.17 percent") — no form encodes one entity's value moving by a delta from one level to another
a fractional magnitude as a measured amount ("11/32") — Fraction exists only as a ProportionOf level, and magnitudes are native numbers
appositional / reformulating 'or' ('$102 million, or 13 cents a share') — the Disjunction section treats every 'or' as inclusive-or-else-Xor and has no equative/restatement sense
a per-share (rate-denominated) restatement of a total — no way to mark two magnitudes as one value expressed on two denominators
a change-over-time differential with an implicit prior value ('up 2 cents') — MoreBy requires two compared entities and there is no licensed 'up/down N from the previous value' form
a measured CHANGE on an event ("rose 2 cents") — Measure records a level on an entity and there is no delta form distinguishing a change from a value
a bond-quote bare fraction as a measured delta ("gained 17/32") — a fractional magnitude on a change-of-value verb has no licensed encoding (same delta gap as tierD-000147)
Financial price-change notation "down 17/32" (32nds of a point) — no licensed form for a bare fraction change whose unit is implicit.

A restrictive relative clause on a group NP ("a handful of companies THAT still make the flu vaccine"): nothing says whether the relative clause becomes a per-member Implication over the group, a group-level event, or rule premises - the only relative-clause guidance is donkey anaphora, which puts a relative clause in a rule's PREMISES.
an index's closing level and its session change ('finished down 31.23 points … at 9,317.64') — Measure requires a surface dimension word for its scale, and 'down' / 'at' supply none

appositive / equative 'or' ('down 27.02, or 0.3 percent') - a restatement of the same quantity in other units, not a disjunction; Disjunction treats every 'or' as inclusive disjunction and has no restatement sense
elliptical apposition of a resulting level ('..., 0.3 percent, 9,321.84,' - the 'to/at' is missing in the source): no dimension word is stated, so the Measure scale has to be invented

Attaching a modifier to one individuated member's own eventuality when only the group event plus the per-member distribution rule were emitted: the instruction set provides no top-level handle on the rule-derived per-member event.
the quantifier word on a plural GROUP subject ("some states") — QuantifierPhrase is defined for kind-level generics and verbal rules, so "some" here goes unrecorded

a stated deadline later revised by the same sentence ("by August, then extended it to Oct. 17") — cessation covers only "no longer / not anymore / used to" for eventualities, and there is no construct for retracting or superseding a time BOUND

a NEGATED generic whose subject and object are both bare kind-denoting NPs ("Ordinary oil does not produce mist-light"): the relational-generic trigger (both arguments bare kind/mass NPs -> an opaque kind-level relation) and the negated-verbal-generic rule ("Ns don't V" -> the distributing Implication at strength 0.0) both apply here, and the instruction set never says which route wins for a transitive negated generic

a restrictive adjective modifying a bare kind NP that fills a kind-level relation slot ('ordinary firelight') — the adjective+noun rule bars fusing incidental description, and its non-fusing split needs a witness, which a bare kind argument does not have
negation of a kind-level relational generic — negation forms are given for copular atoms, event bundles and distributing rules, but never for the opaque two-kind relation

kind-level part-whole inside a generic ('the undersides of nightmoths') — PartOf is defined only over an object's component or a group's member, and a generic definite plural has no group/witness treatment (the determiner rule assumes definite = specific)

negation of a kind-level relational generic — the Negation sections cover copular atoms (strength 0.0 on the same atom) and event bundles (strength-0 And), but nothing states whether 'bare-kind does not V bare-kind' stays the opaque kind relation at strength 0.0 or becomes the strength-0 distributing rule of 'Negated verbal generic'

a restrictive modifier on a bare-kind argument of a kind-level relational generic — the `(Carry mosquito malaria)` form takes bare unmodified kinds, and the instruction set offers no way to restrict such an argument other than minting a fused compound symbol

restrictive adjectival/participial modifier on a bare kind argument of a kind-level relational generic — the adjective+noun rule bars fusing an incidental-description modifier, ConditionalProperty takes a property (not a relation), and there is no other licensed carrier for the restriction

a gerund / nominalized clause in SUBJECT position ("Sky-cats hunting reduces nightmoth populations"): the instruction set has no pattern for an event-denoting nominalized subject, and its one nearby route, the relational generic / kind-level relation, is triggered only by bare kind NPs on both sides

a trigger clause that is itself a bare-plural relational generic ('sky-cats hunt nightmoths'): the relational generic is an opaque kind-level atom with no event witness, so it supplies neither a premise event nor a `During` anchor for the whenever-rule

how a bare-plural clause sitting in an indicative conditional's ANTECEDENT is encoded — as the opaque kind-level relation of Striking & relational generics, or as an event pattern an episodic event can trigger; the conditional rule and the relational-generic rule are stated independently and their interaction is undefined

attributive comparative with an elided standard ('dimmer lights') — the Comparatives section only covers predicative 'X is ADJ-er than Y' / differential / superlative forms and gives no encoding for a comparative modifier with no stated comparand

a bare-kind relational generic carrying a third participant ('to the cliff base') — the kind-level relation form is strictly binary, so a goal PP has no slot and the relational-generic and event-rule routes conflict with nothing to decide between them

a relational generic whose subject kind is restricted by a descriptive adjective and a locative PP ("dead lanterns at the Sunken Cove raise wraiths"): both arguments are bare kind-denoting NPs, which is the stated trigger for the opaque kind-level relation `(Raise <kindA> wraith)`, but no kind symbol is constructible (the compound rules forbid fusing the incidental/damage modifier "dead", and a kind may not occupy LocatedIn's entity slot), and the instruction set never says the distributing-rule route wins in that case

A relational kind-generic with a THIRD, oblique argument: the licensed kind-level relation head is binary (two kind arguments), so "from lit lanterns" has no slot — following the relational-generic trigger drops stated content, and keeping the content requires abandoning the prescribed routing. The instruction set does not say which loss to take.

a restrictive adjectival modifier on a bare-kind argument of a relational generic ("drained lanterns", "weak mist-light"): the trigger is stated as bare kind-denoting NPs on both sides, and there is no rule for carrying a modifier that neither fuses (it is incidental description — damage state, degree) nor may be split off as its own kind-level claim; the distributing-rule alternative with the modifier in the premise is not named as the route

a relational generic with a third, prepositional argument ('Xs ward Ys from Zs') — the kind-level relation form is binary and carries no oblique, while the event-rule route is blocked because both post-verbal NPs are bare kinds too

a kind-level property claim restricted by an NP-internal locative PP ('lanterns in shielded coves'): both the ConditionalProperty locative-restriction rule and the restrictive-modifier-in-rule-premises form are licensed and nothing disambiguates them

a bare-kind relational generic that also carries an oblique ('in the tide-pools'): the kind-level relation is an opaque two-argument atom with no slot for a locative, and the instruction set never says which form wins when the relational-generic trigger fires on a clause with obliques

a deontic norm whose BEARER is an individual but whose OBJECT is universally quantified — the deontic sections cover kind-level bearers (reified property) and specific one-off acts (event `Obligated`), not this mixed case

a kind-level deontic whose verb takes a prepositional ARGUMENT ("must apprentice under a senior Keeper") — the licensed compound action is `verb_object` only, and the ConditionalProperty condition slot is specified for circumstantial restrictions ("at entry"), not for an argument PP, so fusing `apprentice_under_senior_keeper` and hanging (Under …) on it extends the adjective+complement pattern (`sensitive_to_light` + (To …)) to a verb without licence

a permission-granting matrix VERB ("the Council permits an apprentice to V"): whether it is only an ordinary object-control event, or additionally licenses a deontic record on the complement, or (as a standing policy over an indefinite) the kind-level reified permission property, is not addressed — the deontic sections key on a modal or a passive/participial deontic, never on a permitting verb with its own agent

a bare MASS / gerundive activity noun as the SUBJECT of a verbal clause ("Summer hunting yields ..."): the verbal-generic rule form is triggered by a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, and the bare-class-symbol licence is stated only for non-specific OBJECTS, so nothing says whether such a subject becomes a rule range over instances, a kind-level relation, or (as here) a kind constant sitting in the Agent slot of an unmarked event

whether the relational-generic trigger ('both arguments bare kind-denoting NPs' → an opaque kind-level relation) fires when the object is a bare gerundive/eventive nominal rather than an entity kind; on the literal trigger 'Large feather stores enable safe Sunken-Cove tending' would be a kind-level (Enable …) atom, not the distributing event rule emitted here
placing a distributive predicate's per-member rule ("the stations ask") inside a conditional's consequent — the group-plus-distribution machinery is specified only for top-level plural predications

a possessive/comitative "with"-PP modifying a NOUN ("stations with drained lanterns"): "with" is defined only at the event level, split between CoAgent and Instrument, and the entity-attached preposition rules are stated for locatives and for origin "from"
titles-appositives: no carrier for a measured CHANGE on an event ("lower X by N percent") — Measure is absolute, MoreBy compares two entities, and percentages otherwise appear only as (Fraction p 100) inside partitives
'V by N percent' — a percentage extent-of-change on an event has no licensed carrier (Measure is a dimension of an entity, MoreBy a two-entity comparative, Fraction a partitive level)
a gerund clause as the subject of a transitive ('Taking the pill would lower the risk') — the role sections assume entity fillers and never state how an eventuality fills Agent

an adjective's PP complement predicated of a PLURAL/group subject ("the officers were involved in the busts") — the reified-state route anchors on the group, but the prescribed flat copular dual-emit has nowhere to go, since a members' property on the group symbol is barred and the distribution rule carries the state instead
an ordinal on a stage noun ("the final phase") with neither an associated event nor an "-est" dimension to fill `Ordinal`'s scale slot
a phase/stage PP ("in the final phase of a two-year operation") — nothing says whether it is temporal nesting, an interval, or a preposition-named oblique
a content/appositive 'that'-clause complementing a noun ('evidence ... that they really hate Islam')

a possessed plural that is also an event-noun: GroupOf makes the referent a group while the light-verb rule wants that same witness to BE the eventuality carrying Past / Time / Agent, and nothing reconciles the two
a pre-nominal occupational title ("Defense attorney William Rork") — the courtesy-title rule and the appositive rule point different ways and neither is said to govern
comitative "with" naming an inanimate, non-volitional co-participant — `CoAgent` is animate-only and `Instrument` is means-only, so neither role is available
a "with"-phrase naming an INANIMATE co-participant — CoAgent is animate and Instrument is a means, so neither fits and only the preposition-named oblique remains
A title noun premodifying a name ("winner Kelly Clarkson") under a past host — whether the appositive tense-wrapper reaches it is unstated.

The participial reduced relative "starring …" gets no tense of its own; the instruction set fixes the tense of an appositive typing atom but says nothing about a reduced-relative event under a past host.

a proper noun used as a modifier inside a common-noun compound ("his Wimbledon title defence") — the compound rule absorbs it while the naming rule demands its own symbol plus one Name fact, and nothing selects
identity apposition between two co-referring descriptions set off by dashes — the appositive rule covers only typing an entity with a kind, and there is no identity head in the vocabulary
The appositive-wrapper rule is stated inside the copular tense section; that a past VERBAL host also wraps a dash-set appositive's typing atom follows from "past host" but is nowhere spelled out.
the magnitude of a change ('inched up one-tenth of a percentage point') - MoreBy is the gap between two entities, not how far one entity moved
A measured increment of a quantity over time ("rose a tenth of a percentage point"): Measure states a value and MoreBy a two-entity gap; no form covers a delta predicated of a change event.

a verb of formal address whose SOLE object is the addressee ("petitioned a court", "lobbied the agency") — the direct-object change test says Theme, Recipient's addressee-of-communication clause says Recipient

an attributive "with"-PP modifying a common noun ("counties with population declines") — the with-phrase rules are event-side (CoAgent vs Instrument) and the entity-attached preposition licence is framed for position and origin, so nothing states that it extends to an attributed eventuality
Appositive / restatement "or" ("0.70 points, or 0.07 percent" — one change re-expressed in another unit), which the Disjunction section would treat as inclusive disjunction.

`tell` / `inform` — a speech verb taking both a Recipient and a bare (that-less) finite complement — falls outside the attitude verb list, so the holder's role is split between Agent (Thematic roles' progressive test) and Experiencer (the attitudes section), and the sealing treatment is licensed by the section whose role assignment is then not followed.

object-predicative complements of judgment verbs ('hold / consider / deem X responsible', and the agentless passive 'be held responsible') — no section covers a secondary predicate that ascribes a state rather than causing it

not-at-issue appositive content inside a seal ('- the most affected segment -') has no projection route when its anchor is a sealed indefinite, so writer-asserted material stays inside the attitude's scope

the Past wrapper on an appositive competes with the durable reading of a privative descriptor: (Past (Member sorenstam former_winner)) is what the mechanical rule yields, but nothing states how a wrapped privative interacts with its unwrapped genus
party/state appositive abbreviation ("Frist, R-Tenn.") — no rule for expanding abbreviations or encoding political affiliation and constituency

instruction-set tension on the verb "learn": Thematic roles' progressive test lists learn among the eventive mental verbs taking Agent, while Propositional attitudes prescribes Experiencer for its factive list, which includes learn

Ordinal's scale slot for a succession rank among officeholders ('the 25th ... coach') — the scale is defined as the associated event or an explicit -est dimension, and a rank in a series of postholders is neither
abbreviated party-and-state appositive on a legislator's name ('D-W.Va.') — no licensed encoding for its content
An appositive NP carrying its own PP complement ("Democrat of West Virginia"): the appositive yields only a typing atom, so the complement has no witness to attach to.
'the <Placename> N' where the proper noun locates rather than names the referent ('the Birmingham office')

a predicative appositive ('Dahle, a spokesman for the office') yields only a Member atom, so the appositive noun has no symbol for its PP complement to attach to; the Complements-of-nouns rule presumes a noun symbol and the parse has to hang (For …) on the person instead
'one of the [superlative] Ns' as a predicative appositive — Most is unique-superlative only and forKind is the norm-for-a-class construction

a proper-noun (organization) modifier inside a role title before a personal name ('Ahold Chairman Henny de Ruiter') — the compound rules cover adjective and common-noun modifiers, and the title rule covers kinship/courtesy titles only

pre-nominal occupational title ("Board Chairman Henny de Ruiter") — the title rule covers kinship/courtesy titles (title inside the Name string) and the appositive rule gives a host-tensed typing atom; which governs a positional title is unstated

a proper-noun + past-participle pre-modifier ('a US-backed plan') has no stated route: the laminated-worktop rule makes a modifying participle an adjective, while the reduced-relative rule makes it an event, and neither wording addresses the incorporated proper-noun agent
a nominal appositive predicated of a preceding CLAUSE / eventuality ("X began doing Y - an Israeli obligation under Z") — the appositive rule covers only an entity appositive

noun + to-infinitive complement ("plans to expand Wagerup") — the argument-PP rule for nouns names only prepositional complements ("a vehicle for V-ing"), so nothing states the head for an infinitival one
pre-nominal office/role title ('Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi') — the title rule names only kinship and courtesy titles, and it collides with the capitalized-run and appositive-typing routes
controller-role copying into a PASSIVE to-infinitive complement ('deserved to be criticised'), where the controller lands in the complement's object role and not the Agent the control rule names
a pre-nominal title's typing atom has no stated tense rule of its own — the parse borrowed the appositive rule's 'host-clause wrapper', which is stated only for comma appositives
a subject possessive on an event-denoting noun ("Jackson's visit") — the genitive rule offers only PartOf or Possession and never licenses the Agent role the parse uses
percentage as a change amount ("or 8.3 percent") — percentages are covered only as `(Fraction p 100)` inside partitives
appositive / equivalence "or" restating one amount in a second unit, which is not the disjunctive "or" of the Disjunction section
'share X with Y' — the with-phrase is a transfer partner; the two-branch with-test (participant -> CoAgent / means -> Instrument) and Recipient (defined for 'to') do not settle which slot it takes
the "City, State" comma appositive ("Tampa, Fla.") — nested place names in apposition have no stated containment route
A noun-headed measured advantage PP ("with a one-stroke lead over X").
A measured advantage noun ("a one-stroke lead") supplies no dimension word distinct from the noun itself, so Measure's scale slot has to reuse the head noun (lead).
a comitative 'with'-phrase on an event-denoting noun ('a standoff with police') — CoAgent vs collective-Agent is stated for verbal clauses only
a possessive determiner on an event nominalization ('his protest') states the underlying event's agent, but the genitive rule routes it to the opaque Possession, so the agent link is not recorded

whether a state-denoting noun ('shortage') is an event-denoting noun whose witness IS the eventuality — and may therefore carry `Past` / `Time` directly — is unsettled: the light-verb rule names only 'the ceremony' / 'the show' / 'the storm'

instruction-set tension on "say": Thematic roles' progressive test makes a progressive-accepting speech verb an Agent event, while Propositional attitudes prescribes Experiencer for its list (which includes say) — the parse followed the latter

a partitive-looking naming of-phrase that enumerates a definite plural's members ('the cities OF Erbil and Sulaimaniyah') — this is appositive identification, not the possessive, partitive or nominalization-object of-phrase the instruction set distinguishes

a coordinated definite plural filling a single event's NON-Agent role ("a visit to the cities of Erbil and Suleimaniya"): the distributive default would mint one event per conjunct against the singular "a visit", and the collective multi-filler form is specified only for `Agent` on reciprocal/aggregate predicates

a multi-word office title carrying of/for PP arguments ('assistant secretary of energy for defense programs') — Compound concepts licenses only modifier_noun fusion, and nothing says how the complements attach
an occupational/office title before a name ('President Ronald Reagan') — the title rule fixes the Name string but does not say whether a companion kind atom is also licensed

a multi-word office / role title containing internal PPs ('assistant secretary of energy for defense programs'): the compound rules cover only modifier + head-noun fusion and the name rules only capitalized proper names

'then-President Ronald Reagan' — an office title carrying a temporal modifier attached to a name: neither the title rule (title stays in the `Name` string) nor the appositive rule (host-clause-tensed typing atom) carries the 'then-'

an object-predicative role complement ('was appointed <office>'): the state-result shape the parse borrows is written for adjectival results ('painted it red') and for become / turn-into kind change, not for an office conferred by an appointment verb

the role of the appointee: the non-physical-change extension of `Patient` is stated for occurrences and informational artifacts, and does not settle whether a person whose office changes is `Patient` or (by the unclear-case default) `Theme`
"otherwise known as" / alias apposition — two names for one referent, with exactly one Name fact allowed per proper noun and no identity or alias relation defined
a proper-noun modifier naming a distinct possessor ('PeopleSoft management') — the naming section covers name-plus-kind, not a name denoting a separate entity the head noun belongs to
a "known as <quoted term>" nickname appositive: Name carries a string literal for proper nouns only, and the reduced-relative reading would force an odd know event
pre-nominal office title on a proper name ('Florida Speaker Johnnie Byrd'): the title rule names only kinship/courtesy titles, so the stated office survives only inside the Name string

multi-word office title of the form noun + of-PP ('Speaker of the House') — Compound concepts covers only verb_object, phrasal verb and modifier_noun, so neither the fusion nor a genus/of-argument decomposition is specified

a possessed office title predicated of a person ('Florida's Speaker of the House Johnnie Byrd') — nothing states whether the genitive attaches to the office or to the holder, and Possession is the only head available for it

a bare pre-nominal title NP as an appositive ('Speaker of the House Johnnie Byrd') — the appositive rule is stated for the comma form ('Halvard, a wheelwright'), so the tense wrapper for a pre-nominal title is unspecified

a professional / office title fused into the capitalized name run ('County Judge Tim Harley') — the title rule covers kinship and courtesy titles only, and it points the opposite way from the Kestrel-River rule, which mandates a kind atom for a kind word sitting inside a name, so whether (Member tim_harley judge) is due is undetermined
exemplification appositive "N, such as X" — no licensed head or construction

'QVC's management' — the genitive's single test (is the possessed a part / component of the possessor?) is stated for physical components and group membership and does not settle an organizational sub-unit, so `Possession` vs `PartOf` is undetermined here

a proper-noun modifier inside a compound NP ("the QVC management team") — Compound concepts explicitly does not apply to proper nouns, so the part-whole route to (PartOf sk_team_1 qvc) is improvisation

a bare-plural relational-noun subject restricted by "of the" ("Members of the QVC management team") has no designated encoding — Partitives require a cardinal or non-universal proportional amount, and the explicit-universal route requires every/each/all
journalistic party-district apposition 'D-Waco' — no covered encoding; the parse drops it
abbreviated party-and-district appositive on a legislator's name ('D-Waco')
an honorific abbreviation ('Rep.') in the `Name` string — the title rule names kinship and courtesy titles, not professional/office abbreviations, though the same treatment plainly extends

'allow X to V' as a control/permission verb: the control-verb pattern names try/want/decide/…, so whether the permitted event attaches by `Theme` with the object controller copied in as its `Agent` is an extension, not a stated rule
reformulative/appositive 'or' ('$4, or 17.2 percent') restating one quantity in another unit rather than disjoining — `(Or …)` would be wrong and nothing else is offered
a percentage as a measure unit: `(Fraction p 100)` exists only in `ProportionOf`'s level slot, so a relative magnitude on a `Measure` cannot be expressed

being 'in' an event or competition stage ('in the third round', 'in the final') — participation has no head of its own; only the framing-PP route ('in fluid mechanics' -> the preposition-named In) comes close

extent-of-change stated as a percentage on a change verb ('increased 3.3 percent') — Measure presumes a stated scale and a physical unit, while (Fraction n 100) is reserved for partitive proportions of a definite set, so no licensed form fits squarely
'or' as an appositive restatement of one value in another unit ('9.05 points, or 0.94 percent') — the Disjunction section would wrongly make this an opaque (Or …)
a definite plural proper noun naming party members ("the Democrats") - nothing chooses between a group witness over a lowercased kind and a name-derived symbol plus its mandatory Name fact

the implicit agent of a nominalization supplied only by an attributive modifier ("Republican efforts" - who does the forcing) has no licensed carrier once the modifier is barred from minting a referent

What projects out of a seal beyond the typing atom — a definite NP inside an attitude complement may carry a possessor, an appositive and a clausal complement, and only `Member` / `Name` (and `GroupOf`) are named as projecting.
"including" as an appositive-inclusion marker on an NP, as distinct from the reduced-relative reading — though the instruction set's expansion test does decide it for drifted participles.
appositive / equative 'or' ('$13.1 million, or 22 cents per share') - one amount restated, and the Disjunction section has no non-disjunctive sense of 'or'

appositive / equivalence 'or' restating one amount in a second unit (points vs percent)
an alias / ticker appositive ('.SPX') for an already-named entity, where a proper noun is allowed exactly one Name fact

an occupational/role title as an honorific ('Manager Lloyd McClendon') — the title rule covers kinship and courtesy titles only, leaving it unsettled whether 'Manager' stays in the Name string or becomes a typing atom

pre-nominal office title carrying its own place argument ('Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan'): the title rule covers only kinship/courtesy titles and offers no way to attach the jurisdiction to the office

appositive / reformulating "or" ("42.56 points, or half a percent") restating one quantity in another unit — only the inclusive and exclusive senses are defined

privative / temporal adjectives on a role noun ('former manager', 'ex-', 'would-be') — no encoding is defined, and the cessation bundle is explicitly scoped to 'no longer / not anymore / used to'
a bare numeral age predication ('was 26') — Measure wants a stated adjective or dimension noun and a stated unit

"another N": one-anaphora covers "a red car … a blue one" but nothing records the distinctness from an earlier, unmentioned instance that "another" asserts.
"another N" — distinctness from a salient antecedent has no carrier (one-anaphora covers "one", not the exclusion "another" adds)
a discourse-deictic 'That' pointing at a preceding sentence with no CONTEXT supplied — no antecedent exists to reuse and no licensed way to record the pointing

A restrictive relative clause on a group NP ("a handful of companies THAT still make the flu vaccine"): nothing says whether the relative clause becomes a per-member Implication over the group, a group-level event, or rule premises - the only relative-clause guidance is donkey anaphora, which puts a relative clause in a rule's PREMISES.

a possessive pronoun bound by a distributed coordinated subject ("Kroger ... and Albertsons ... locked out their union workers") -- the coordination rule says a shared object reuses one symbol, but says nothing about a possessum that co-varies with each conjunct; the parse split it into two disjoint worker groups

"the next morning" with no antecedent event anywhere in the text: the term-propagation rule assumes an antecedent whose day terms can be incremented and which the new event can be ordered after with Before, so with none supplied the "next" shift is silently lost and only the day-part survives.

a proper-noun modifier on a common noun ('Reuters witnesses') — Compound concepts does not apply to proper nouns and the genitive rule requires 's or a possessive pronoun, so nothing licenses an attachment between the name and the head noun
first- and second-person pronouns ('our', 'we', 'I', 'you') — the anonymous-witness rule classes he/she/it/they only, and nothing licenses linking the speaker into a 'we' group

an anaphoric definite that supplies a kind for an already-named referent ('the company' -> apple_computer) — coreference is specified as pure symbol reuse, so it is unclear whether a (Member apple_computer company) typing atom should be added; none is emitted and the named entity carries only its Name atom

an anaphoric demonstrative plural with no antecedent ('of those') — the antecedent-less-pronoun rule covers he/she/they/it but not demonstratives, so nothing fixes the member kind of the presupposed superset
kind-anaphoric 'that kind of N' / 'this sort of N' — no way to record the anaphoric link back to a previously described kind
plural demonstrative 'those' with an antecedent outside the passage — the anonymous-witness defaults cover he/she/it/they, so the member kind (person vs thing) is unspecified
the indefinite pronoun 'others' — the no-antecedent pronoun rule enumerates only he/she/they/it, leaving the group's member kind undetermined
an unbound PLURAL pronoun with an inanimate referent ("them" = the records) — Names and casing fixes (GroupOf sk_group_1 person) for plural they with no "salient kind" escape, unlike singular "it"

indicative 'if <clause>, <clause>' conditional: named only in passing ('a plain Implication rule', in the counterfactual subsection) with no worked example, and no statement of how an indefinite subject in the antecedent ('a lantern') is bound — as the rule's range variable, or as the witness that the Existential section prescribes for an indefinite under a verbal predicate
an anaphoric definite ('the mist-light') pointing back at a bare mass-noun object, which the instruction set would store as a bare class symbol, leaving no witness for the definite to reuse

indicative 'if P, Q' conditional — the instruction set names the plain Implication form but gives no worked example, so nothing fixes how the antecedent clause's event and participants are variabilized, nor whether the consequent's per-occurrence Skolem event ties back to the antecedent (the During tie is specified only for 'every time / whenever')

Bare plural objects: the instruction set fixes bare plural SUBJECTS (generic kind, `Inheritance`) and definite/demonstrative plurals (group witness), but states no rule for a bare plural in object position.

a quantifier word ('many') on an NP inside a conditional antecedent: the QuantifierPhrase companion's (kind, verb-lemma, word) shape does not fit a rule that ranges over occurrences, the strength channel is already occupied by the rule's own reliability, and 'many' is listed as a proportion word rather than one of CardinalityPhrase's vague-count phrases

Bare "few" as a determiner on the subject of a conditional's antecedent: the instruction set maps "few" to strength 0.1 (which here would wrongly weaken the whole conditional rather than count the moths), and the CardinalityPhrase lexicon lists only "a few / several / a handful / dozens / scores / hundreds / a lot of"; neither channel is prescribed for this position.

how a bare-plural clause sitting in an indicative conditional's ANTECEDENT is encoded — as the opaque kind-level relation of Striking & relational generics, or as an event pattern an episodic event can trigger; the conditional rule and the relational-generic rule are stated independently and their interaction is undefined

a proportional quantifier ('few') on a NON-subject argument inside a conditional's antecedent — the strength + QuantifierPhrase channel is defined only for the quantified subject of a generic (setting rule strength here would wrongly say the rule holds rarely), so a low-proportion object NP has no licensed carrier

an indefinite introduced inside a whenever-trigger ("a lit lantern") that the main clause picks up as a definite ("the lantern") - the whenever template shows only definite constants, and quantifier-bound anaphora is given only for relative clauses (donkey anaphora)

indicative conditional 'If <event clause>, <generic clause>' — the instruction set says only that it is a plain Implication rule and shows no worked example, so nothing fixes whether the antecedent clause's event and participants must be rule variables (vs. witness constants), nor whether the consequent's per-occurrence event links back to the antecedent occasion
an indefinite ('a lantern') inside a when/whenever rule's trigger clause — the Skolem machinery is specified for existentials in rule CONCLUSIONS only, and no form is given for one in the antecedent

a demonstrative definite in a conditional's consequent that co-varies with the antecedent ("that lantern" = the lantern the wintergloss burns in): an antecedent-less definite is given a fresh constant, with no way to make it depend on the rule variable

an indefinite subject inside such a conditional antecedent ('a senior Keeper retires') — Existential says an indefinite with a verbal predicate is a witness and that a verbal generic needs a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, but a conditional antecedent gives it universal force with no stated encoding

"many" as a determiner counting things inside a conditional's antecedent: it is listed as a proportion word (strength 0.7, which here would wrongly weaken the whole conditional) and is absent from the CardinalityPhrase vague-quantity lexicon, so neither channel is prescribed for this position.

a recurring indicative conditional whose antecedent is a STATE rather than an event ("If the moon is full, the Council meets ..."): the occurrence-quantifying form indexes the consequent event to a trigger variable, but a variable-free premise leaves no binding to index on, and the instruction set never expands its own plain-Implication conditional example to atoms, so the consequent event's form (constant vs occurrence-indexed) is unsettled

contrastive-anaphoric temporal adjunct 'at other times' — Time takes structured calendar terms or deictic/named time constants, and there is no rule for a complement-set temporal NP (the parse mints the constant other_time and fuses 'other'+'time' although 'other' is incidental, not a classifier)

A capitalized proper-noun modifier on a lowercase common-noun head where the name denotes a distinct possessor entity ("the Watch ledgers" = the ledgers of the Watch). The Kestrel-River / Brindle-estuary rule would make the ledgers themselves the entity named "Watch"; the noun-modifier compound rule would fuse watch_ledger and bury the name; and the Possession branch is defined only for 's, possessive pronouns and genitive of-phrases, not for a bare noun-noun compound. Which route applies is unaddressed.

a frequency adverb inside a conditional antecedent ('if Ns V often, ...') - the two licensed channels for a frequency adverb (the rule's strength and the QuantifierPhrase companion) both belong to an asserted generic/habitual, and neither can express 'often' as a condition on the antecedent

an indicative conditional with an indefinite in its antecedent — the Counterfactual section routes 'if X, Y' to 'a plain Implication rule' but never says which antecedent constituents become $-variables and which stay witness constants

bare habitual "When <clause>, <clause>" with a copular antecedent over a definite referent: the instruction set gives the occurrence rule only for "every time / whenever", ConditionalProperty only for a kind's own property under a condition, and the indicative-conditional Implication with no worked internals, so the rule's shape (variable-free premise, Skolem term keyed on a constant) has no stated model
purpose-result-inf: 'meaning that P' - a clause-level elaborating participle relating two propositions has no licensed head; the connective lexicon is closed to cause / purpose / concession / contrast, so the relation can only be dropped

a purposive connective head outside the seeded PurposeOf lexicon (InAnEffortTo) — the explanation-question bridge is defined only over To / InOrderTo / SoAsTo, so "what did they petition for?" cannot bind through this atom even though the head is licensed by the open surface-connective rule
a sentence-initial frame adverbial ('For legal purposes, ...') has only the event-level oblique to attach to, so it lands inside the strength-0 denial and reads as denied content
an adjective with an infinitival complement ('ready to go') — the complement rule covers PP arguments only
"with the capacity to V" — a noun with an infinitival ability complement; Can is stated only for "can / able to"

noun + to-infinitive complement ("plans to expand Wagerup") — the argument-PP rule for nouns names only prepositional complements ("a vehicle for V-ing"), so nothing states the head for an infinitival one
result / consequence infinitive ("rose ... to close at ..."), distinct from the purpose infinitive that licenses `To`

the implicit subject of a purpose infinitive ('devised a mini-lift to allow …') — the purpose-infinitive rule fixes the connective head and clause order but not who fills the purpose event's subject role

the implicit subject (controller) of a purpose-infinitive ADJUNCT is unspecified — the subject-control default is stated only for control-verb complements, leaving 'devised a lift to allow X to Y' with two coherent controllers and no rule

A purpose / result INFINITIVE modifying a NOUN ("efforts to force ..."): the purpose-infinitive rule is written for a clausal adjunct on an action, and the noun-complement pattern is stated only for "for".
result/outcome infinitive ('weakened ... to trade at X') — the only licensed 'to V' head is the purpose infinitive, whose seeded PurposeOf derivation would misreport it
result/extent infinitive ('rebounded to trade at …') — the infinitive rules cover purpose and control complements only
Result infinitive ('to end at $28.12'): only purpose infinitives (To / InOrderTo) are covered, and result-vs-purpose is not distinguished.
Result/outcome infinitive ("dropped ... to close at X"): only purpose infinitives take the To head, and no head records a non-purposive outcome.

A noun with a to-infinitival complement ('ways to end world hunger'): the noun-complement section covers of-phrases and prepositional arguments, and the purpose head To is defined between two events, so nothing squarely licenses an infinitival complement on a noun's own symbol.

The infinitive marker 'to' is not a preposition, so the entity-attached surface-head convention does not strictly cover it; whether an entity-first (To <noun> <event>) is the same head as the event-to-event purpose connective To is unspecified.
Result infinitive 'to yield 4.067 percent' off a stative predication: To needs an eventuality in its first argument.

Even with the connective-endpoint reification trigger available for the host state, a complement encoded as a Measure predication supplies no eventuality for To's second argument, so the result infinitive has no endpoint on either side.
specificational copular with an infinitival complement ("our preference is to achieve X") — no encoding for "N is to V"

purposive adjunct headed by a noun ("in an effort to V", "in a bid to V"): the connective section names only "to" / "in order to" / "so as to" as purpose heads, while the noun-complement section would instead make "an effort" a witness with a To-complement, and nothing selects between them

a sentence-initial frame adverbial scoping over the whole statement ('For legal purposes, ...') — only event-level obliques exist, so it can only be attached to the event and thereby falls inside the strength-0 denial, reading as part of what is denied
an adjective with an infinitival complement ("ready to go") — the complement rule covers PP arguments only, and the control-verb pattern is stated for verbs

"with the capacity to V" — a noun with an infinitival complement expressing ability; Status predicates license Can only for "can / able to", and the noun-complement section covers of-phrases and "for"-arguments, not a periphrastic ability noun

a 'for NP to VP' infinitival clause with its own overt subject as a prepositional verb's complement ('wait for legal hurdles to be crossed') — the control-verb rule covers only subject/object-controlled to-infinitives
noun + to-infinitive complement ('plans to expand Wagerup') — the instruction set covers argument PPs on nouns ('a vehicle for V-ing') but gives no head for an infinitival complement
result / consequence infinitive ("rose ... to close at ..."), distinct from the purpose infinitive that licenses the `To` head

a means/method gerund adjunct ("won X by winning Y") relating two events — the connective section covers cause, purpose, concession and contrast but not manner-of-achievement "by V-ing", and Instrument is restricted to a tool or substance

the implicit subject of a purpose infinitive ("devised a mini-lift to allow ...") -- the purpose-infinitive rule fixes the connective head and clause order but says nothing about who fills the purpose event's subject role; the parse chose the artifact rather than the matrix subject
coordinated non-finite complements under one matrix verb ('allow X to board and descend') — the coordination rule addresses clauses/VPs and NPs, not shared-matrix infinitival conjuncts

a noun's to-infinitive complement ("efforts TO force ...") — the noun-complement section covers of-phrases and "for" arguments but not a to-infinitive on a nominalization, and it is not the purpose-infinitive case either since there is no main clause action

A purpose/result INFINITIVE modifying a NOUN ("efforts to force …") — the purpose-infinitive rule is written for a clausal adjunct on an action, and the noun-complement pattern that would fit is stated only for "for".
result / outcome infinitive ('weakened ... to trade at 55.34/39'): the only 'to V' rule is the purpose infinitive (To / InOrderTo), which this is not - the currency does not weaken in order to trade
Result / extent infinitive ("rebounded to trade at …") — the infinitive rules cover purpose (`To`) and control complements (`Theme`), not a resultant-state infinitive.
Result infinitive ('to end at $28.12' = and so ended): only purpose infinitives (To / InOrderTo) are covered, and result-vs-purpose is not distinguished.
result/outcome infinitive ("dropped ... to close at X") — only purpose infinitives are given the To head, and no head records a non-purposive outcome

a noun with a to-infinitival complement ("ways to end world hunger") — the noun-complement section covers of-phrases and prepositional arguments on nominalizations, and the purpose-infinitive head To is defined only between two EVENTS, so nothing licenses an infinitival complement hanging off a noun's own symbol
Result infinitive "to yield 4.067 percent" hanging off a stative measure predication rather than an event — `To` needs an eventuality in its first argument.
specificational copular with an infinitival complement ('our preference is to achieve X') — no encoding for 'N is to V'
during-synonym: 'in an interview' — an occasion NP as the object of 'in': Location is defined for 'in / at / on', During renders only the word 'during', and the preposition-named oblique is the residue; no rule decides which an event-denoting object takes

a circumstantial "in <event-noun>" (an occasion, not a place or a domain) has no dedicated head: Location is spatial, During renders only "during", and the preposition-named oblique is gated on aboutness/directedness

plain simultaneity "when" joining two simple-past clauses — the time sections assign canonical forms to after/before/during/while but none to bare "when", so the link between the incident beginning and the call is lost

simultaneity 'when' joining two clauses — temporal connectives take no connective atom, but no canonical form is named for simultaneity (During covers during/while/throughout), so the begin event and the reported call stay temporally unrelated
temporal "as" as a simultaneity subordinator — the temporal list names after / before / when / while / until / as-soon-as, and only during / while / throughout map to During
an event-denoting NP as the object of locative 'at' ('at the meeting') — Location/LocatedIn are specified for places, and During renders only 'during / while / throughout'

a durative-span preposition outside during / while / throughout ("through the holiday") — the surface-preposition oblique is the licensed head, but it sits outside the `During` eventuality-nesting form, so one relation has two possible spellings

a simultaneous temporal "when"-clause has no assigned head (only Before / BeforeBy / During are named), and here the eventuality it modifies sits inside an attitude seal that ordering atoms may not cross

participation-'in' whose object is itself an eventuality ('compete in the third round'): the preposition-named oblique records the PP, but nothing temporally nests the two eventualities, since During is reserved for the surface word 'during'
'in morning <X> trade' as a market/session frame — Time, Location, In and During each mis-describe it; the repair uses In on the state witness as the least-wrong licensed form

'the first hour of trading' - an ordinal-selected sub-interval of an activity: Ordinal is defined for entity ranks on an event or an '-est' scale, and the of-phrase is neither genitive, partitive nor a during-nesting
"during" with a time-period NP as its object ("during its first week of operation") — During is defined as nesting one eventuality inside another, and a week is not an eventuality

Plain simultaneity 'when' joining two simple-past clauses: the connective rules name Before/During as the canonical forms for after/before/during/while but assign none to bare 'when', so the temporal link between the incident beginning and the deputies receiving the call is simply lost.

simultaneity 'when' joining two clauses — the instruction set bars a connective atom and sends temporal connectives to 'the time sections', but names no canonical form for simultaneity (During is defined only for during/while/throughout), so the begin event and the reported call are left temporally unrelated

Temporal "as" as a simultaneity subordinator ("as the world champion relaxed"): the temporal-connective list names after/before/when/while/until/as-soon-as, and only during/while/throughout are mapped to During; bare "as" is never addressed.
an event-denoting NP as the object of locative 'at' ('at the meeting') — Location/LocatedIn are specified for places and During renders only 'during / while / throughout'

a simultaneous temporal "when"-clause: only Before / BeforeBy / During are named for temporal connectives and no head is assigned to "when"; here the eventuality it modifies (the dragging) sits inside an attitude seal, and ordering atoms may never cross a seal boundary
simultaneity 'when'-clause ('When X was V-ed, Y V-ed'): the time section fixes canonical heads for after/before/during/while, but names none for plain 'when' outside the past-perfect (Before) case
an event-nominalization used as a circumstantial frame ('in trading on the Nasdaq market') — the nesting head During is licensed only for during/while/throughout

clause-level participial complex prepositions ('based on X', 'according to X', 'due to X'): the reduced-relative rule covers participles post-modifying a noun, and the -ing preposition list (during/pending/notwithstanding) does not reach these
"in <event-noun> trade" as a temporal/market frame — the licensed obliques (Time, Location, In) and the During relation all mis-describe it

'the first hour of trading' - an ordinal-selected sub-interval of an activity: Ordinal is defined for entity ranks on an event or '-est' scale, and the of-phrase is neither genitive, partitive nor a 'during' nesting
'during' with a time-period NP as its object ('during its first week of operation') — During is defined as nesting one eventuality inside another, and a week is not an eventuality

a gerund / nominalized clause in SUBJECT position as the argument of a matrix verb ("Lighting a lantern produces mist-light"): the instruction set reifies embedded eventualities only in COMPLEMENT position (causation-flavored verbs, control verbs, perception reports) and gives no route for an event-denoting subject, nor for quantifying over it generically, so the choice between an Agent role on the produce event and a whenever-style rule with During is unsettled

generic conditional headed by bare 'when' ("When a N Vs O, the N Vs O") — the Implication-rule form is given for 'every time / whenever' and for indicative 'if', while 'when' is listed only among the temporal connectives that keep their Before/During forms, so which route a generic 'when'-clause takes is unspecified

generic 'When <clause>, <clause>' conditional: the instruction set names 'every time / whenever' (rule + per-occurrence Skolem + `During`) and indicative 'if' (plain `Implication`), but never says which route a bare 'when' takes

Generic "when <clause>, <clause>" conditional: "when" is listed among the temporal connectives that keep their time-section forms, while only "every time / whenever" (an occurrence rule whose response is tied to its trigger with During) and indicative "if" (a plain Implication) get rule treatments; which of these a bare generic "when"-clause takes, and whether a During link is owed, is not addressed.

indicative 'if P, Q' conditional — the instruction set names the plain Implication form but gives no worked example, so nothing fixes how the antecedent clause's event and participants are variabilized, nor whether the consequent's per-occurrence Skolem event ties back to the antecedent (the During tie is specified only for 'every time / whenever')

whether an ordinary indicative "if P, Q" inherits the whenever-rule's `During` link, or only the plain `Implication` — the counterfactual section routes it to "a plain Implication rule" without saying which parts of the occurrence-quantifying machinery come along

generic conditional headed by bare 'when' ("When Ns V, the Ns V") — the Implication-rule form is given for 'every time / whenever' and for indicative 'if', while 'when' is listed only among the temporal connectives that keep their Before/During forms, so which route a generic 'when'-clause takes is unspecified

habitual/generic 'when <clause>, <clause>': the occurrence-quantifying rule is specified for 'every time / whenever' only, while bare 'when' is listed among the temporal connectives that take the canonical time forms (`Before`/`During`) — the instruction set does not say which route a generic 'when' takes

a trigger clause that is itself a bare-plural relational generic ('sky-cats hunt nightmoths'): the relational generic is an opaque kind-level atom with no event witness, so it supplies neither a premise event nor a `During` anchor for the whenever-rule

'during the day' — a 'during' adjunct whose object is a bare time-span NP rather than an eventuality: the `During` operator is defined as nesting one reified eventuality inside another, and the day-part list on `Time` enumerates morning/afternoon/evening/night without 'day', so this adjunct has no directly stated encoding
durative "through the night": the extent reading over a time-of-day NP has no carrier — day-parts are point-like `Time` symbols and During is defined only between two reified eventualities

a generic "When P, Q" conditional with indefinite subjects: the occurrence-quantifying rule (with its During link) is licensed only for explicit "every time / whenever", and bare indicative "if" is routed to a plain Implication, leaving generic "when" unassigned between the two forms

temporal proximity to a named time or lunar phase ("occur near new moon"): the Time section offers Time / Before / BeforeBy / TimeAtLeast / TimeAtMost / During but no nearness relation, so the parse falls back on the entity-attached spatial-preposition head for what is a temporal relation

temporal-proximity adjunct ("occur near the new moon"): Time carries calendar/deictic terms, Before/BeforeBy carry ordering and During carries containment, but nothing encodes "close in time to <event or recurring phase>"

a period-extent adjunct ('through winter') — no licensed form for 'throughout <named period>': During needs a reified eventuality, Start/End need structured terms, and seasons have no structured Time term at all

temporal 'through/throughout + a bare time-span noun' ('through winter') as the extent of a state - During needs a reified outer eventuality, Time records the season but drops the extent, and Start/End need structured terms, so no licensed head carries it

generic 'When <clause>, <clause>' — 'when' is listed among the temporal connectives that keep their Before/During forms, while the occurrence-quantifying rule form is specified only for 'every time / whenever', so nothing decides which route a bare habitual 'when' takes

a frequency-adverb generic whose occasions are restricted by a bare-plural temporal adjunct ("rarely V on cold nights"): nothing says whether the restriction becomes a rule premise or a dependent existential in the consequent

a trigger clause that is itself a bare-plural relational generic ('sky-cats hunt nightmoths'): the relational generic is an opaque kind-level atom with no event witness, so it supplies neither a premise event nor a `During` anchor for the whenever-rule

a descriptive modifier on a plural inside a RULE PREMISE: the prescribed remedy for 'never predicate a member property of the group symbol' is the distributive rule, which is defined for asserted statements and has no stated form for restricting a premise-bound group to members with that property

An indefinite object under a negated verbal generic ("Ns do not V a ADJ N"). The instruction set says an indefinite argument is an existential witness, and under a generic rule a dependent existential is a Skolem function inside the consequent; it gives no treatment of the negation's scope, where the natural reading is universal (no wraith approaches any warded lantern). The parse takes that universal reading by lifting "a warded lantern" into a second premise, a form no worked example covers.

a descriptive (non-fusing) modifier on a BARE-PLURAL generic subject ("fresh ... feathers ward ..."): the instruction set specifies the split for a definite plural (distribute per the copular rule) and for a kind (fuse or leave separate), but never states that on a verbal generic the modifier becomes an extra premise restricting the rule's range, which is what this parse did
